title: Should the Fouled Player Take the Penalty Himself?
excerpt: A player gets fouled by the keeper and walks straight to the spot. Should he? Theory says no: he's jarred and wound up while the keeper is locked in. We tested it on 79 such penalties against 3,456 others in Europe's top 5 leagues.
finding: When the fouled player takes the penalty himself, 75.95% go in against 78.96% for everyone else: 3 points lower, but with only 79 such kicks the data can't yet say 'hand it to someone else'.

title: Not All Goals Are Equal: A Time-Aware Expected-Points Model
excerpt: A goal from 0–0 to 1–0 in the fifth minute and the same goal in the eighty-fifth are not the same thing. Expected points prices every goal by the scoreline it changes and the minute it lands, estimated from every minute of 13,206 matches in six top-flight leagues.
finding: A go-ahead goal from level is worth 2.05× as much in the last 15 minutes as in the first, in every league and in seasons the model never saw. No player's timing stands out from chance.

title: The True Contributors: Who Actually Moves the Table?
excerpt: Every goal priced by the points it was worth and shared with the scorer, the assister and the pass before. Who adds the most per 90 once luck and short careers are allowed for, and how sure can anyone be?
finding: Only two players are sure of a top-10 place for expected points added per 90: Messi and Mbappé. From number 3 down, the ranking is far less settled than any "best player" list suggests: Neymar, third on the best estimate, could plausibly rank anywhere from 1 to 34.
